# `prefer-min-max`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports conditional `if` expressions choosing the lesser or greater of two
operands that can be expressed directly with `@min` or `@max`.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Zig provides `@min` and `@max` as standard built-in functions. They clearly
express bounds, clamping, and extrema directly, work across integer and float
types, are vectorized, and avoid repetitive conditional branching.

## When it fires

Whenever scalar values are compared to select the lesser or greater value.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn smaller(a: u32, b: u32) u32 {
    return if (a < b) a else b;
}
```
